description: Fail-closed inventory of every runtime or collector root required before lua_rust may sweep a live VM.

provenance_audit.implemented: GcRef carries a process-global non-reused ObjectId; each collector validates address, ObjectId, and concrete tag in an authoritative live table. LightUserdata is a separate arbitrary-pointer type, and collector explicit roots retain erased pointer + ObjectId + tag handles.
provenance_audit.remaining_sweep_blocker: Runtime safe-point full and incremental collection consume the canonical tracer, prepare finalizers, retrace resurrected graphs, reconcile weak tables, pre-close unreachable coroutine states, sweep the object graph, and deliver protected callbacks. Production managed-object mutations use a checked post-write barrier and a separate fail-closed inventory. Broader transitional non-string GcRef::as_ref call sites, allocator live/peak accounting, and allocation-triggered automatic collection remain open.

owner.current: Runtime's unique Heap owns the GarbageCollector and canonical StringPool under one HeapId. The collector stores erased pointer + ObjectId + concrete tag root handles; ObjectId is process-global and never reused.
owner.target: Heap owns scoped RootToken entries with HeapId and generation validation.

tracer.current: RuntimeRootTracer calls begin_mark_only, which validates every root's address, ObjectId, and tag against the collector live table before header access, then labels seeded and rejected collector roots without dereference.
tracer.target: RuntimeRootTracer seeds validated collector roots and labels them with RootKind.

root_kinds.missing_risk: Unique Heap lifetime, address-reuse provenance, full STW, and explicit incremental tracer integration are closed, but persistent explicit-root storage still lacks lexical RootToken generations; allocation-triggered automatic collection remains gated.

planned_test.assertion: A registered explicit root is marked, foreign/stale roots are rejected before dereference, and a stale ObjectId cannot validate when the same address is test-injected with a replacement identity.

owner.current: GarbageCollector::with_publication provides a higher-ranked PublicationTxn and branded Rooted handle. New allocations and protected call-result slices enter an ObjectId-bearing temporary-root registry before exposure; panic/nested-scope Drop removes exact identities. Compiler Proto graphs, standard-library/package/IO construction, VM Table/closure/string/open-Upvalue temporaries, Runtime roots/errors, CLI argument buffers, and synchronous call/top-level result consumption remain protected until an explicit root, traced state/Table, or active Lua stack owns them.

source_locations.symbol: coroutine create/wrap transactional State to Thread publication

owner.current: StateArena inserts a detached coroutine into a slot carrying an exact nonzero temporary-root identity. A branded PendingState is the only safe commit capability; Drop rolls an unpublished slot back and advances or permanently retires its generation. Coroutine create/wrap keep Thread, Upvalue, and wrapper objects protected while installing checked State -> Thread and Thread -> StateHandle edges, then release the state root only after direct stack publication.
owner.target: Runtime publication owns a branded PendingState that rolls the arena slot back unless State-to-Thread publication commits.

tracer.current: RuntimeRootTracer snapshots validated temporary StateHandles independently from ordinary arena membership and object-publication roots, labels them TEMPORARY_STATE_ROOTS, and feeds them into the state/object fixed-point queues.
tracer.target: RuntimeRootTracer seeds validated temporary StateHandles independently from temporary GC-object roots.

root_kinds.missing_risk: This root kind is locally complete for coroutine create/wrap. Full and explicit incremental collection consume the canonical tracer and pre-sweep only untraced owned states; allocation-triggered automatic collection remains blocked by broader scoped object access and allocator accounting.

planned_test.name: pending_state_rolls_back_or_publishes_atomically
planned_test.assertion: GC/failure injection between arena insertion, Thread allocation, binding, and stack publication either preserves the state through commit or removes the slot and advances/retire its generation exactly once.

owner.current: The unique RuntimeStorage lifecycle owns Heap and NativeActivationStack together. It retains every active RuntimeRequest, deferred native frame, caller/target Thread edge, continuation snapshot, ordinary/debug open-Upvalue transfer, GC maintenance/finalizer frame, and pending response until delivery; NativeActivationSessionGuard restores links and drains the buffer on success, error, or panic.
owner.target: The unique Runtime owner exposes the activation buffer as a canonical root provider to full and incremental collection.

tracer.current: RuntimeRootTracer invokes NativeActivationStack::seed_roots and labels the provider. It marks request arguments, Thread handles, caller Proto, saved active stack/call-frame values, yielded/error values, debug Upvalue/name/write payloads, GC request/current-finalizer/response edges, and pending responses at every state-turn boundary before the next state is borrowed.
tracer.target: RuntimeRootTracer labels activation-buffer edges and invokes the provider during every stop-the-world and incremental root seed.

root_kinds.missing_risk: Lua-visible full, explicit incremental, and allocation-triggered automatic collection call this canonical provider after releasing the current state turn, including during finalizer reentry. Cross-state finalizer resume/open-Upvalue transfers remain deliberately fail-closed.

planned_test.name: runtime_native_activation_roots_survive_switch_delivery_and_unwind; debug_upvalue_operations_schedule_cross_state_and_protected_calls
planned_test.assertion: Request arguments, debug Upvalue/name/write payloads, continuation values, pending results/errors, and caller/target Threads remain marked while peak borrowed StateArena slots stays one; success, protected delivery, VM error, and panic all leave the activation buffer empty.
